<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,400;9..144,600&family=DM+Sans:wght@400;500;600&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600&display=swap">
<style>
:root{--paper:#FAF7F1;--ink:#211C16;--ink-2:#4F473C;--muted:#7C7365;--rule:#E4DCCB;--rule-2:#EFE7D9;--tint:#F3EFE6;--accent:#1A5E6B;--accent-2:#5FB0BC;--pass:#2F6B4F;--pass-bg:#E6F0EA;--defect:#A93B2C;--defect-bg:#F6E7E3;--absence:#9A6B1F;--absence-bg:#F5EBD6;--shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(33,28,22,.06),0 10px 24px -18px rgba(33,28,22,.35)}
@media (prefers-color-scheme:dark){:root:not([data-theme="light"]){--paper:#16120E;--ink:#EFE7D9;--ink-2:#CFC5B3;--muted:#ABA294;--rule:#33291F;--rule-2:#2A2119;--tint:#1F1913;--accent:#5FB0BC;--accent-2:#1A5E6B;--pass:#7BBF9A;--pass-bg:#1B2E25;--defect:#E0836F;--defect-bg:#3A211B;--absence:#D9A64A;--absence-bg:#382C16;--shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.3),0 10px 24px -18px rgba(0,0,0,.8)}}
:root[data-theme="dark"]{--paper:#16120E;--ink:#EFE7D9;--ink-2:#CFC5B3;--muted:#ABA294;--rule:#33291F;--rule-2:#2A2119;--tint:#1F1913;--accent:#5FB0BC;--accent-2:#1A5E6B;--pass:#7BBF9A;--pass-bg:#1B2E25;--defect:#E0836F;--defect-bg:#3A211B;--absence:#D9A64A;--absence-bg:#382C16;--shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.3),0 10px 24px -18px rgba(0,0,0,.8)}
*{box-sizing:border-box}
body{margin:0;background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);font-family:'DM Sans',system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:15.5px;line-height:1.55;-webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased}

:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px}

.mono{font-family:'JetBrains Mono',Menlo,monospace;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}

h1{font-family:'Fraunces',Georgia,serif;font-optical-sizing:auto;font-weight:600;font-size:clamp(34px,4.6vw,52px);line-height:1.02;letter-spacing:-.015em;margin:8px 0 12px;text-wrap:balance}
h2{font-family:'Fraunces',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:26px;line-height:1.15;letter-spacing:-.01em;margin:0 0 6px;text-wrap:balance}

.strip .n{font-family:'Fraunces',Georgia,serif;font-size:30px;font-weight:600;line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}

.rail .door{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--muted);margin-top:8px;line-height:1.4}

table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:13.5px}

.v{display:inline-block;font-family:'JetBrains Mono',Menlo,monospace;font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;font-weight:600;padding:2px 7px;border-radius:2px;white-space:nowrap}
.v.pass{color:var(--pass);background:var(--pass-bg)}.v.defect{color:var(--defect);background:var(--defect-bg)}.v.absence{color:var(--absence);background:var(--absence-bg)}
code{font-family:'JetBrains Mono',Menlo,monospace;font-size:.9em;background:var(--tint);padding:1px 5px;border-radius:2px}

.findings{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:14px 0 0;display:grid;gap:10px}
.findings li{display:grid;grid-template-columns:64px 1fr;gap:14px;padding:12px 14px;border:1px solid var(--rule);background:var(--paper)}
.findings li.blocking{border-left:4px solid var(--defect)}
.findings .id{font-family:'JetBrains Mono',Menlo,monospace;font-weight:600;font-size:13px;color:var(--defect)}
.findings .id.absence{color:var(--absence)}
.findings .body{font-size:14px}
.findings .body b{font-weight:600}
.findings .where{display:block;font-family:'JetBrains Mono',Menlo,monospace;font-size:11.5px;color:var(--muted);margin-top:4px;word-break:break-all}
.probe{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(200px,1fr));gap:0;border:1px solid var(--rule);margin:14px 0 18px}
.probe>div{padding:12px 14px;border-right:1px solid var(--rule)}.probe>div:last-child{border-right:0}
.probe .k{font-family:'JetBrains Mono',Menlo,monospace;font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--muted)}
.probe .val{font-size:14px;margin-top:4px}
.callout{border-left:3px solid var(--accent);padding:6px 16px;margin:16px 0;color:var(--ink-2);max-width:70ch}
.not{columns:2;column-gap:32px;font-size:13.5px;color:var(--ink-2);max-width:none}
.not li{break-inside:avoid;margin-bottom:6px}
footer{margin-top:44px;padding-top:16px;border-top:1px solid var(--rule);font-size:12px;color:var(--muted)}
@media (max-width:760px){.phase{grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:12px}.rail{position:static}.rail .step{font-size:30px}.not{columns:1}}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{transition:none!important}}
</style>
<div class="wrap">
<header>
  <div class="eyebrow">Mudavym · POS → inventory → alerts lens, and the morning after · measured 2026-09-03</div>
  <h1>Sim Meyhouse, One Friday</h1>
  <p class="dek">The real Meyhouse Palo Alto menu, hours and prices, run through Mudavym's own doors as a new owner would: load the cellar, program the POS, ring a service, then read every screen back against the database — that night and the morning after.</p>
  <div class="meta">
    <span>Tenant <span class="mono">a229f22b-2aac-4e54-a8b2-033a8f93ac5e</span></span>
    <span>Gateway <span class="mono">main + PR #285</span></span>
    <span>Service rang <span class="mono">22:29–23:20 PDT</span> — after the venue's 22:00 Friday close; nothing warned</span>
    <span>Writes: product UI and API only · Database: read-only checks</span>
  </div>
</header>

<div class="strip">
  <div><div class="n">53</div><div class="l">inventory items loaded · 308 bottles, all priced from the printed menu</div></div>
  <div><div class="n">135</div><div class="l">POS buttons programmed · 5 oz / 8 oz / bottle / rakı single / double</div></div>
  <div><div class="n">44</div><div class="l">checks closed · 9 on the terminal, 35 through the SimPOS API · 99 lines, 1 void</div></div>
  <div><div class="n pass">34</div><div class="l">bottles depleted by sale · 55 consumption rows · double-close refused</div></div>
  <div><div class="n absence">$0</div><div class="l">"Value on hand" shown for a 308-bottle cellar · 52 of 54 lots carry no cost</div></div>
  <div><div class="n defect">2 of 7</div><div class="l">low-stock alerts that reached the inbox · the alert ledger says all 7 were sent</div></div>
</div>

<section class="phase">
  <div class="rail"><div class="step">1</div><div class="door">Load the cellar</div><div class="rule"></div><div class="door">Doors: Add Wine, Receive a delivery (bulk), Count</div></div>
  <div>
    <h2>A count creates real stock — worth nothing</h2>
    <p>The onboarding question was whether a physical count on an item with zero stock actually brings stock into existence, or only records a number. Measured: it creates a lot. The count row is written unconditionally, then <code>apply_stock_movement</code> runs on the non-zero delta and inserts an <code>inventory_lots</code> row at <code>unit_cost NULL</code>, provenance <code>estimated</code>. So an opening count is a legitimate door for a cellar that was never bought through the product — but the stock it creates is valued at nothing until a receipt revalues it.</p>
    <div class="probe">
      <div><div class="k">Probe</div><div class="val">Heras Cordon, Rioja 2017 · 0 lots → count 7</div></div>
      <div><div class="k">inventory_lots</div><div class="val">+1 row · qty 7 · <span class="mono">unit_cost NULL</span> · estimated</div></div>
      <div><div class="k">inventory_transactions</div><div class="val">reconciliation / mobile_count · 0 → 7</div></div>
      <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="val mono" style="font-size:12px">inventory.service.ts:363,405 → record_stock_count (20260902190000:275-303) → lot_cost_truth:163-166</div></div>
    </div>
    <p>The good door is the bulk one: <code>POST /inventory/:rid/items/bulk</code>, the same call "Receive a delivery" makes, took 50 free-text menu lines, resolved them against the Master Library, created provisional rows for wines it had never seen, and failed on none — in 42 seconds. The Add Wine modal is the weak one: it pre-fills "Cost per Bottle" from another restaurant's reference price and cannot express <em>I don't know</em> — a cleared field becomes <code>0</code>, and the API then labels that zero as typed by a person.</p>
    <div class="figs">
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Inventory page before anything exists"><figcaption><span class="mono">01 · /inventory</span>The honest empty state, before the cellar exists.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Add Wine configure pane with cost pre-filled"><figcaption><span class="mono">04 · Add Wine → Configure</span>"Cost per Bottle" arrives pre-filled at $90 from the shared library. There is no way to say the cost is unknown.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Inventory after the bulk receive showing value on hand $0"><figcaption><span class="mono">09 · /inventory after the bulk receive</span>53 wines, 308 bottles — and "Value on hand $0", because unknown cost renders as zero.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
    <p style="margin-top:14px">What a real owner could not do: keep a spirits list (every row, five rakı included, is typed "Red"; the library is a wine library); price one wine at two pour sizes (one <code>pour_size_ml</code> per item, while all 22 by-the-glass wines print 5 oz and 8 oz); or sell food through SimPOS at all.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="phase">
  <div class="rail"><div class="step">2</div><div class="door">Program the POS</div><div class="rule"></div><div class="door">Doors: SimPOS "Edit POS", catalog API</div></div>
  <div>
    <h2>Every seeded button costs $45</h2>
    <p>SimPOS seeds its catalog from the cellar on first load. Fifty-three buttons appeared, all priced $45.00 — a fallback literal in the seeding code, unmarked on screen. Thirty-nine were repriced by hand to the printed menu; the rest of the 135 buttons (5 oz glass at 148 ml, 8 oz at 237 ml, bottle, rakı single and double) were typed through the same catalog door the Edit POS form uses. The form has no category: a meze becomes a 750 ml wine.</p>
    <div class="figs">
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="SimPOS terminal on first load with every button at $45"><figcaption><span class="mono">10 · /simpos/:id on first load</span>Tables 1–20 greyed "coming soon"; the seeded catalog, every price $45.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="SimPOS menu with 135 programmed buttons"><figcaption><span class="mono">14 · the programmed menu</span>135 buttons at printed-menu prices, glass sizes as separate buttons — the way a real POS is set up.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="phase">
  <div class="rail"><div class="step">3</div><div class="door">Ring the service</div><div class="rule"></div><div class="door">Doors: terminal UI, SimPOS check API</div></div>
  <div>
    <h2>Forty-four checks, one void, one refused double-close</h2>
    <p>Lunch two-tops with a glass each, dinner four-tops with a bottle and mezes, a six-top sharing a bottle of rakı, a whole-table tasting menu, two 8 oz pours, a void, a button that exists on the menu but not in inventory, and one check closed twice — which the terminal correctly refused with a 403 and no second ledger row.</p>
    <p>Before a single bottle could move, the POS buttons had to be connected to stock. There is no screen for that anywhere in the product: the SPA calls two POS-hub routes, <code>providers</code> and <code>status</code>. The mapping endpoints exist and work, so 107 mappings were approved one by one through the API — none of the 135 auto-matched, because the trigram similarity tops out at 0.88 against a 0.9 threshold — and seven of those approvals were rejected mid-queue by the rate limiter. Even an approved match cannot deplete on its own: it carries no sale unit or volume, so the next line landed as <code>no_sale_volume</code> until a second, equally invisible queue was worked.</p>
    <div class="figs">
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Open check with three lines before Order"><figcaption><span class="mono">17 · check 1</span>Two 5 oz pours and a meze on the open check, before Order.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="SimPOS order log listing 45 checks"><figcaption><span class="mono">24 · /simpos/:id/orders</span>45 checks with lines and prices, webhook "sent". No check total anywhere; times shown in the viewer's zone, not the venue's.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="phase">
  <div class="rail"><div class="step">4</div><div class="door">Read it back</div><div class="rule"></div><div class="door">Every surface against the database</div></div>
  <div>
    <h2>What the screens said, against what the rows hold</h2>
    <div class="scroll"><table>
      <thead><tr><th>Surface</th><th>Rendered</th><th>Database</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td><code>/inventory</code> settled</td><td>53 wines · 274 bottles on hand</td><td class="num">53 items · SUM(lots.qty) 274</td><td><span class="v pass">match</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/inventory</code> value on hand</td><td><b>$0</b> cost basis; every row VALUE $0</td><td class="num">52 of 54 lots unit_cost NULL</td><td><span class="v absence">absence as $0</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/inventory</code> below-par chip</td><td><b>9</b>, 2 critical</td><td class="num">/low-stock and /summary → 7, critical 0</td><td><span class="v defect">two definitions</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/inventory</code> first 2.5 s</td><td>"0 wines, 0 bottles" · "$0" · "Showing 0 of 0"</td><td class="num">53 / 274</td><td><span class="v absence">loading = empty</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/simpos/:id/orders</code></td><td>45 checks, lines, prices, webhook sent</td><td class="num">simpos_checks 45 · lines 99</td><td><span class="v pass">match</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/notifications</code></td><td>"7 Wines Need Restocking" naming all 7; 1 item in the stream</td><td class="num">notifications 2 rows · 3 wines · 7 below par</td><td><span class="v defect">stream missed 4</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/dashboard</code></td><td>Active Inventory 53 · 274 bottles · 205.5 L; Low Stock 7</td><td class="num">matches</td><td><span class="v pass">match</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/dashboard</code> vendor spend</td><td>$0 ↗ +0.0% vs last month</td><td class="num">no purchase orders exist</td><td><span class="v absence">green arrow over nothing</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/reports</code></td><td>"Sales revenue needs a connected POS and is not shown here"; KPIs — —</td><td class="num">44 pos_checks · 34 depleted · 55 consumption rows</td><td><span class="v defect">wrong cause</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>/recommendations</code></td><td>12 rules evaluated · 1 active: Muhammara + Köpoğlu co-occur 2.2× chance</td><td class="num">true of tonight's checks</td><td><span class="v pass">correct</span></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table></div>
    <div class="scroll"><table>
      <thead><tr><th>Ledger and POS totals</th><th>Database</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td><code>pos_checks</code></td><td class="num">44 — total, subtotal, tip, covers, table_id, server_name NULL on 44 of 44</td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>pos_unresolved_lines</code></td><td class="num">39 — unmapped 38 (mezes and coffee, declared "wine"), no_sale_volume 1</td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>wine_consumption_log</code></td><td class="num">55 — 40 glass, 15 bottle</td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>inventory_transactions</code></td><td class="num">89 — initial/manual 52 · sale/pos 34 · reconciliation/mobile_count 3</td></tr>
        <tr><td><code>pos_item_mappings</code></td><td class="num">107 — all through the API, 0 through any screen</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table></div>
    <div class="figs">
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Inventory page loading state showing zero wines"><figcaption><span class="mono">25 · /inventory, first 2.5 seconds</span>"0 wines, 0 bottles on hand" while the database held 53 and 274. Captured twice, minutes apart. Byte-identical to an empty cellar.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Inventory page settled after service"><figcaption><span class="mono">32 · /inventory settled</span>53 wines, 274 bottles, "Below par 9" against an API that says 7; every row valued $0; rakı typed "Red".</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Notifications page after service"><figcaption><span class="mono">26 · /notifications</span>"7 Wines Need Restocking" names all seven by live read; the notification stream holds one — four crossings were ledger-marked as alerted and never sent.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Dashboard the morning after"><figcaption><span class="mono">27 · /dashboard</span>Inventory figures match the rows. "Vendor Spend $0 ↗ +0.0%" — a green trend over a base that does not exist.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Reports page saying sales revenue needs a connected POS"><figcaption><span class="mono">28 · /reports</span>"Sales revenue needs a connected POS" over 44 ingested checks. Honest about the gap, wrong about the cause.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Recommendations page with one basket-affinity insight"><figcaption><span class="mono">30 · /recommendations</span>One insight, true of tonight's checks, honest about its denominator: 12 rules evaluated, 1 active.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="phase">
  <div class="rail"><div class="step">5</div><div class="door">The morning after</div><div class="rule"></div><div class="door">What the product knows about the night — read as the owner, and as a guest where a door exists</div></div>
  <div>
    <h2>True, false, and missing</h2>
    <p>The same tenant the next morning: 53 items, 44 checks, 55 consumption rows, two notifications. Every intelligence surface was read against the rows. Three claims held to the dollar; two were false; three things a manager would ask for were missing.</p>
    <div class="scroll"><table>
      <thead><tr><th>What an owner is told</th><th>Verdict</th><th>Evidence</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>53 items in active inventory · 7 wines need restocking</td><td><span class="v pass">true</span></td><td>match the rows; One-Tap Actions names the seven correctly</td></tr>
        <tr><td><em>Which</em> seven wines, from the Low Stock card</td><td><span class="v defect">false</span></td><td>"Unknown wine", blank counts — the card reads camelCase from a snake_case payload</td></tr>
        <tr><td>$2,236 of wine sales tonight</td><td><span class="v absence">buried</span></td><td>exact to the dollar in Reports' Consumption Analytics; never a headline; the same page says "no sales data" above it</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Promote the Muhammara + Köpoğlu pairing</td><td><span class="v pass">true</span></td><td>12 rules evaluated, 1 active, grounded in the night's checks; the other 11 rendered nothing</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Two alerts from the night</td><td><span class="v defect">one shown</span></td><td>both keyed to one stack by delivery mode; the Alvear Solera 1927 alert never renders</td></tr>
        <tr><td>"30 orders this month"</td><td><span class="v defect">false</span></td><td>zero orders exist; the badge counts the thirty days of the window</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Ask the sommelier what sold best, what to reorder</td><td><span class="v absence">missing</span></td><td>honest "currently unavailable" on all four questions; the offline fallback can never fire</td></tr>
        <tr><td>A guest asks for a Turkish red for lamb under $80</td><td><span class="v absence">no door</span></td><td>no guest-facing route exists; the only public page is a vendor's B2B catalogue</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table></div>
    <div class="figs">
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Dashboard the morning after with Unknown wine on every low-stock card"><figcaption><span class="mono">01 · /dashboard</span>Inventory tiles match the rows; the Low Stock card renders "Unknown wine" seven times over a payload that carries the names.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Notifications page showing one of two alerts"><figcaption><span class="mono">05 · /notifications</span>"TODAY (1)" over two real rows — the second alert is folded into the first.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Recommendations page with one grounded insight"><figcaption><span class="mono">03 · /recommendations</span>The healthy surface: one recommendation, true of the night, and nothing invented for the eleven rules that found nothing.</figcaption></figure>

The fallback that could have answered from inventory never runs.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
    <div class="callout">The one page that says what it did not read: Logs — "Read 5 of 6 registers · not read: the event store", with POS 44 matching the checks exactly. That sentence is the shape every other surface should have.</div>

</section>

<section class="phase">
  <div class="rail"><div class="step">6</div><div class="door">The invoice, in our template</div><div class="rule"></div><div class="door">ADR 0104 slice 2, behind the Mudavym gate · extraction supplied from Claude Code because the gateway's model key has no credit</div></div>
  <div>
    <h2>Three synthetic documents through the real door, rendered as one canonical document — twice</h2>
    <p>The corpus was empty, so three documents that say "SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE" in their own text went through the product's intake door on the sim tenant: a Turkish wine-distributor invoice with KDV and a returnable-deposit line, a California distributor invoice with CRV, freight and sales tax, and a Turkish delivery note with no money. The gateway's own extractor could not run, so this session read each PDF and supplied the extraction through a new guarded door, in the extractor's own JSON contract. The page is the same component for all three; sections appear by document type. The first render named nine findings; they were fixed the same day and the invoices were re-issued as second versions and rendered again — the Turkish sheet below is the third render, after one more arithmetic fault the second render exposed was fixed the same day.</p>
    <div class="figs">
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Turkish invoice, second version, rendered as the canonical document"><figcaption><span class="mono">Turkish invoice SYN-TR-0002 · third render, after the deposit fix</span>Seller, buyer and delivered date carried; the VAT row reads "20% on ₺9.172,00"; the deposit is one coded 7161 charge and the ladder now agrees with the paper: Lines ₺9.172, Charges ₺180, Before tax ₺9.352, Tax ₺1.834,40, Total ₺11.186,40. The verdict says "Not compared — no order or door count to compare against", which is the truth of a document that sits on no delivery.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="California invoice, second version, rendered as the canonical document"><figcaption><span class="mono">California invoice SYN-US-0002 · after the nine fixes</span>Freight and CRV as coded charges, sales tax as a breakdown row, delivered date; lines, charges, tax and total agree to the cent.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Turkish delivery note in the door view with no prices"><figcaption><span class="mono">Delivery note SYN-IRS-0001 · door view</span>No money anywhere on this screen; every "received" says "not counted" in words, none is a zero.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
    <div class="scroll"><table>
      <thead><tr><th>What the first real render showed</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Verdict block reported absence as difference ("4 lines differ" with nothing to compare)</td><td><span class="v pass">fixed</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td>Seller dropped, buyer blank, delivered date and VAT breakdown missing from the extraction contract, charges not summed, deposits uncoded</td><td><span class="v pass">fixed</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td>"The original cannot be brought" — the premise was wrong: all five originals were stored and sign; the corpus counter had listed one folder placeholder</td><td><span class="v absence">corrected</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td>A deposit stated as a line and as a subtotal was counted twice in the ladder — the stated subtotal (which contained the deposit) won over the computed goods total; now measured and corrected, and a computed-versus-stated mismatch is named in the verdict</td><td><span class="v pass">fixed</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td>The page and the corpus runner mapped a stored document two different ways; one mapping now serves both, and the corpus run names five historical failures on the first-version documents and none on the second</td><td><span class="v pass">fixed</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td>Price base, as-printed strings, "not counted", the honest tie-out line, the money-less door</td><td><span class="v pass">held</span></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table></div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="phase">
  <div class="rail"><div class="step">7</div><div class="door">A second venue, a second currency</div><div class="rule"></div><div class="door">Vanilla, Kaleiçi, Antalya · Europe/Istanbul · main at 528f13d1</div></div>
  <div>
    <h2>Vanilla, Kaleiçi: a cocktail bar's Saturday in lira</h2>
    <p>The second venue was chosen because its menu is published as data, not an image: 284 priced rows in ₺ across cocktails, spirits, wines, beers, soft drinks and food, plus Google's measured popular-times curve (Saturday 20:00 is the peak; Friday is the second-quietest day). Nothing was estimated that the venue does not publish: no seat count exists anywhere, so no covers were derived. The bar was onboarded through the same doors as Meyhouse — 27 wines loaded (the library is a wine library, so the 46 cocktails and 78 spirits have no home in inventory), 268 POS buttons in lira, 38 checks rung on the Saturday curve.</p>

        <tr><td><code>/notifications</code></td><td>20 unread · critical card with 7 Meyhouse wines</td><td class="num">this tenant owns 1 notification; 27 of 28 belong to two other restaurants</td><td><span class="v defect">scoped to user</span></td></tr>

    <p style="margin-top:12px">Two of these became founder decisions the same day: below par is strictly below par (a wine at par is at par), and a generic, producer-less name stays the venue's own provisional wine — only a specific identity joins the shared library, and nothing is renamed under a venue. Both are being built now, alongside the fixes for the inbox scoping, the asserted type, the fabricated producer and the unpriced row.</p>

      <li><span class="id">F8</span><span class="body"><b>Raising a par level raises no alert.</b> Three pars raised above stock through the product's own PATCH door → 0 notifications; the 2-minute sweep caught two of them nine minutes later.<span class="where">inventory.service.ts (hook only at :330, :451) · low-stock-alerts.service.ts:102</span></span></li>

<section class="phase">
  <div class="rail"><div class="step">9</div><div class="door">Vendor lens</div><div class="rule"></div><div class="door">Doors: door count, deliveries, proposals, agree, verify · 2026-09-06 · PR #329</div></div>
  <div>
    <h2>A short delivery, argued to AGREED and VERIFIED through the doors — and one gate that lets a difference through unanswered</h2>
    <p>Slices 1–3 of the agreed-invoice work are on main. The Turkish second-version invoice was counted at the door as 10 of 12 on line 1, a delivery was created (UNORDERED: nothing ordered it), the invoice and the delivery note were linked, and the product said so: <i>differs from the vendor's paperwork on 1 line</i>. The restaurant proposed SHORT_SHIP, the vendor countered with a ₺142,00 credit, the restaurant accepted, and the delivery reached AGREED under rule A — both sides on the record — then VERIFIED by a named person. Stock and cost were not touched: 0 inventory transactions, 0 lots, as the door itself says.</p>
    <p>Every gate was then tried the wrong way. Agree with one side only → 409 <i>"Silence is not agreement here"</i>. Agree with a proposal still open → 409. Verify before AGREED → 409. Propose on a VERIFIED delivery → 409. A second verify → 201, same timestamp.</p>
    <div class="figs">
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="01 · the door frame on invoice SYN-TR-0002"><figcaption><span class="mono">01 · the door frame on invoice SYN-TR-0002</span>Line 1 counted as 10 of 12 with a synthetic photo attached; the count is a receiving_advice document, source manual — the door's own write, not an edit of the invoice.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="02 · the delivery spine"><figcaption><span class="mono">02 · the delivery spine</span>Delivery 65e450cf, provenance UNORDERED, with the invoice and the delivery note linked under their roles.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="03 · the notification"><figcaption><span class="mono">03 · the notification</span>"Differs from the vendor's paperwork on 1 line(s)" — delivery_differs, differingLines 1, through the notifications door.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="04 · proposal thread and gates"><figcaption><span class="mono">04 · proposal thread and gates</span>SHORT_SHIP proposed from the restaurant side, the vendor's counter with a ₺142,00 credit, accepted; agree and verify with their gates explained on screen.</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="05 · the canonical document, delivery linked"><figcaption><span class="mono">05 · the canonical document, delivery linked</span>The same invoice page after AGREED → VERIFIED; our own door count appears under Billed while Received still reads "not counted" (finding V3).</figcaption></figure>
      <figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="06 · the door frame after verification"><figcaption><span class="mono">06 · the door frame after verification</span>Verified by a named person; a second verify returned the same verified_at.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
    <ul class="findings">
      <li><span class="id pass">V1 ✓</span><span class="body"><b>Founder's call, built and re-driven live the same day (PR #330, ADR 0103 A11).</b> A fresh door count (10 of 12) on a new delivery: agree → 409 <i>"1 recorded difference has no answer — line 1 of the door count (10 against 12)"</i>; after the restaurant's explicit accept-as-billed on that line → AGREED under rule A → VERIFIED. The identical count sent twice → 409 naming the existing document (V4 ✓).</span></li>
      <li><span class="id pass">V5 ✓</span><span class="body"><b>An acceptance keyed to a line that has no recorded difference was written and reported as accepted</b> — it answered nothing, and agree still refused. Found live, fixed the same day (PR #331) and re-driven live: the wrong key → 409 naming the one difference that can be answered; the right key → 201 → AGREED.<span class="where">deliveries accept-as-billed door · lens-vendor/a11-live.json</span></span></li>
      <li class="blocking"><span class="id">V1</span><span class="body"><b>A delivery flagged as differing reached AGREED in one call with no proposal.</b> Rule A checks that both positions exist, never that a recorded difference was answered. Measured on delivery 2e26cc6a before the intended sequence; the full sequence was rerun on 65e450cf. This is an ADR 0103 D3 amendment — the founder's call.<span class="where">v3.0-TECH-DEBT.md 2026-09-06 · ADR 0103 review trail</span></span></li>
      <li><span class="id pass">V2 ✓</span><span class="body"><b>Founder's call: stock at the door, cost at VERIFIED (PR #333, ADR 0103 A1/A5, A12).</b> Re-driven live after the merge: a door count naming a shelf booked 10 bottles (stock 17 → 27, one transaction); a line naming no shelf was reported "not booked" with the reason and moved nothing; VERIFIED left the lot <i>provisional</i> because the invoice line names no item — "a cost nobody agreed is not a final cost". 162 lots that carried no price at all were backfilled from a false <i>final</i> to <i>provisional</i>.
